title: The Day Virgin Atlantic Flew Its Only Plane to Newark
conflicts: Origin: Branson's own retellings (CNBC 2019, Virgin Atlantic site) start with his call to Boeing and omit Fields; Gale and BTN say Fields approached him in February/early 1984. Story gives both, attributed. Fields's exit terms disagree: The Herald calls it a severance settlement of lifetime first-class travel; David Spanier (Independent) says he sold his share for lifetime free travel; Wikipedia's £125,000 compensation and £1m buyout could not be confirmed in a loadable source, so the story names only the free travel and no date. Fields's original concept: Gale says all-business-class, BTN says flights to the Falklands; story uses Gale only.
notes: The bird-strike/engine story from Branson's memoir is omitted (no loadable source); the story uses BBC reporter John Bell's recollection of an unscheduled engine change the day before the first flight. Branson's blog on virgin.com blocks automated requests.
